comments.content: `isFalsy` is not the negation of `isTruthy`: for `null` both return `false`. In `Assert.run`, a render that yields `null` therefore falls into the success branch (`isFalsy(null) == false`), so a condition that produces no boolean value is silently counted as a passing assertion — the opposite of what the task is for. Other callers (e.g. `FilterItems`, `ExecutorService`) explicitly guard against the null case, which shows the asymmetry is easy to hit. Implement it as the complement of `isTruthy` so the two helpers have a consistent contract.

public static boolean isFalsy(String condition) {
        return !isTruthy(condition);
comments.existing_code:
public static boolean isFalsy(String condition) {
        return condition != null && FALSE_VALUES.contains(condition);

content: "`getExpression()` returns the raw, un-rendered property value, so the list is parsed before any templating happens.
